runs.question: How did engine_getBlobs response time scale with blob count for each execution client on mainnet on 8 June 2026 (UTC)?
runs.answer:
From `mainnet.int_engine_get_blobs` for June 8, 2026 (142,684 SUCCESS observations), `engine_getBlobs` response time scales **roughly linearly** with blob count for all 6 EL clients, but with very different slopes:

| EL Client | Scaling slope (avg ms per blob) | ~P95 at 6 blobs | ~P95 at 12 blobs | ~P95 at 18 blobs |
|-----------|------|------|------|------|
| **Reth** | ~0.8 ms/blob | 12 ms | 24 ms | 23 ms |
| **Nethermind** | ~1 ms/blob | 29 ms | 55 ms | 57 ms |
| **Ethrex** | ~1.2 ms/blob | 18 ms | 24 ms | 32 ms |
| **Besu** | ~2 ms/blob | 32 ms | 70 ms | 46 ms |
| **Geth** | ~8 ms/blob | 81 ms | 158 ms | 232 ms |
| **Erigon** | ~8 ms/blob | 76 ms | 135 ms | 201 ms |

**Key findings:**
- **Reth** is the fastest at every blob count, with avg ~2ms at 1 blob and ~23ms at 21 blobs
- **Nethermind** is close second, ~1.6ms at 1 blob, ~24ms at 21 blobs  
- **Geth** and **Erigon** have the steepest scaling — ~8ms avg per additional blob, reaching ~179ms at 21 blobs
- All clients show near-linear scaling, but the constant factor varies by ~10x between fastest (Reth) and slowest (Geth/Erigon)

- **P95 response time**: [getblobs_p95_scaling.png](http://127.0.0.1:2480/api/v1/storage/files/6488702edd99/f1f76517-264c-46a0-bb17-a6b9cc1cda5b/getblobs_p95_scaling.png)

runs.question: How much does block payload size affect block propagation time on mainnet?
runs.answer:
**Block payload size has minimal effect on block propagation time on mainnet.**

Based on 50,272 blocks from the last 7 days:

| Size Range | Count | Avg (ms) | P50 (ms) | P95 (ms) |
|-----------|-------|---------|---------|---------|
| <50KB     | 2,032 | 1,375   | 1,344   | 2,453   |
| 50-100KB  | 6,174 | 1,611   | 1,451   | 2,949   |
| 100-150KB | 10,845| 1,726   | 1,501   | 3,002   |
| 150-200KB | 10,968| 1,782   | 1,530   | 3,049   |
| 200-250KB | 8,666 | 1,813   | 1,552   | 3,070   |
| 250-300KB | 5,592 | 1,882   | 1,618   | 3,103   |
| >300KB    | 5,994 | 1,921   | 1,647   | 3,142   |

**Key findings:**
- Pearson correlation: **r = 0.17** — a very weak positive correlation
- Going from the smallest (<50KB) to the largest (>300KB) blocks, median propagation rises only **~300ms** (from 1,344 to 1,647 ms)
- P95 propagation grows by ~700ms across the range
- Even the largest blocks (>300KB, up to 849KB) propagate in under ~3.1s P95

**Conclusion:** Block payload size plays a minor role in propagation time. Other factors — geographic distance between peers, client implementation, network topology — dominate the variance. The gossip layer handles large blocks efficiently, with only ~300ms median penalty for the biggest blocks.

runs.question: Around the 3rd-4th of December 2025, MEV relay circuit breakers reportedly tripped on mainnet and relay-delivered blocks collapsed for a while. Find the actual window and quantify how bad it got.
runs.answer:
Here are the findings:

## Window

The crash started around **2025-12-04 02:50 UTC**, was worst between **03:00–04:59 UTC**, and recovery was underway by **~05:00 UTC**, back to normal by **~05:30 UTC**.

## Severity

| Metric | Baseline (Dec 1-3) | Worst 2h (03:00-04:59) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Relay-delivered blocks/hr | ~277/hr | **77/hr** | **−72%** |
| Relay share of all blocks | ~96% (typical) | **35.6%** (154 of 433) | validators fell back to local blocks |
| Worst 5-min bucket | ~23 blocks | **1 block** (04:30, 04:55, 03:25) | −96% |

Multiple 5‑minute buckets saw just **1 relay-delivered block** vs. the normal ~23. Every major relay was affected — BloXroute Max Profit delivered the most (61) during the worst 2h but was still far below normal; Flashbots managed only 5, Aestus 12, Titan 26, Agnostic Gnosis 4. Bids were still flowing (100k–400k/relay per 15min) but the relays' block‑delivery circuit breakers were tripping, forcing proposers to build locally.

runs.answer:
Here are the findings:

## Window

**Dec 3, ~21:00 UTC → Dec 4, ~09:00 UTC** (~12 hours), with the **nadir at Dec 4, 03:00–04:00 UTC**.

## Timeline

| Hour (UTC) | Canonical blocks | Relay-delivered | Relay % | Orphans | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dec 3 18-20 | ~298/hr | ~273/hr | **92%** | 0–1 | Baseline |
| Dec 3 21:00 | 288 | 266 | 92% | 0 | First subtle dip (10 slots missing) |
| Dec 3 22:00 | 279 | 240 | 86% | 2 | Clear drop begins |
| Dec 3 23:00 | 285 | 266 | 93% | 2 | Brief partial recovery |
| Dec 4 00:00 | 289 | 264 | 91% | 3 | Still degraded |
| Dec 4 01:00 | 288 | 250 | 87% | 3 | |
| Dec 4 02:00 | 281 | 238 | 85% | 9 | Orphans rising |
| **Dec 4 03:00** | **217** | **77** | **35.5%** | **7** | **Collapse** |
| **Dec 4 04:00** | **216** | **77** | **35.6%** | **24** | **Worst orphan spike** |
| Dec 4 05:00 | 262 | 212 | 81% | 19 | Recovery begins |
| Dec 4 06:00 | 277 | 243 | 88% | 9 | |
| Dec 4 07:00 | 276 | 235 | 85% | 7 | |
| Dec 4 08:00 | 276 | 239 | 87% | 10 | |
| Dec 4 09:00 | 284 | 251 | 88% | 4 | Near normal |

## How bad it got

- **Relay share collapsed** from ~92% of canonical blocks to **35.5%** — a **61% relative drop**.
- At the worst, only **77 blocks/hour** were relay-delivered vs a normal ~273 — **72% fewer relay blocks**.
- **~280 slots** in the 03:00–04:00 window had **no relay delivery** at all (proposers fell back to local blocks).
- **Orphan rate exploded**: 24 orphans in a single hour (04:00) vs a normal 0–2 — a **12–24× spike**.
- **Full-day Dec 4 toll**: 6,765 canonical blocks vs normal ~7,140 = **~375 missing blocks** (5.2% miss rate vs normal <0.3%). Relay-delivered blocks dropped to 5,802 vs normal ~6,600.
- **Relays most affected**: Flashbots went from ~628 blocks on Dec 3 to ~17 in the first 2 hours of Dec 4; Aestus from ~446 to 13; Agnostic Gnosis from ~652 to 32. Ultra Sound and Titan Relay held up relatively best.

The circuit breakers tripped in **cascade starting around Dec 3 21:00 UTC**, likely triggered by a chain event that caused relays to see conflicting head views. The **deepest freeze was Dec 4 03:00–04:00 UTC**, with recovery extending through ~09:00 UTC.
